title: One owner for each piece of state
outcome: Separate source state, derived values, URL state, server data, and temporary UI state.
version: Portable JavaScript · React hooks · Vue 2/3 comparisons · Next App Router

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: A component stores tasks, filter, and visibleTasks. Updating a task forgets to update visibleTasks. Repair the model.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: A delete disappears optimistically, then fails. What must the UI remember?

trace.title: User action
trace.detail: Source state is information you choose to store. Derived state can be calculated from it. If tasks and a filter are stored, visibleTasks can often be derived. Storing both copies creates a synchronization job you may not need.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Begin with the user action. Editing a draft changes local unsaved state. Saving asks the server to change persisted state. A successful response updates the cached server record. A derived list recalculates from that cache and the URL filter.

For optimistic UI, record how to undo or reconcile a failed action. If two saves overlap, an old response must not erase a newer edit. A disabled button alone may not cover every caller.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: Copying props into local state once can make later prop changes invisible. Deriving everything in an effect adds extra updates and stale intermediate renders. Define ownership and reset rules first.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Separate source state, derived values, URL state, server data, and temporary UI state. Give a concrete failure example.
